name: Dusty Pink
lede: Dusty Pink is a muted, slightly bluish rose; the word *dusty* means a color with grey mixed in, and the name sits beside old rose and antique pink.

sections.title: Dusty and old
sections.body: St Clair defines old rose as a dusty pink with blue undertones [1]; the two names belong to one family with [[dusty-rose]] and [[antique-pink]]. The swatch is in the ISCC-NBS 1955 list as block 29 and in Ridgway's 1912 atlas, and its nearest ISCC-NBS name is "dark pink", 4.8 units away [2]. That makes it a close neighbor of [[ruber]], with grey added.

sections.title: A pink nose on a goat
sections.body: Finlay, crossing the 5,360-metre Chang La pass in Ladakh, spotted a herd of mostly white goats of the kind that give fine cashmere wool; he noted their dusty pink noses [3]. It is a small case of the name being used for a living thing.

sections.title: The word in print
sections.body: In printed English, *dusty pink* peaks in the 1940s and rose fastest in the 1930s, in Google Books, counting every sense of the words [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: It appears in 29 of 23,781 archive paintings, 0.12 per cent, rarer than 70 per cent of named colors [5]. The earliest dated example is from 1560, but the archive's early centuries are thin, so that date is a floor, not a first [5]. Among 15 dated paintings with at least 2 per cent of the canvas, the latest is from 1909 [5]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings [5].
